query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount of copper (approximately 1–2 atomic percent) to (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 will promote the in situ formation of ductile nanoprecipitates along grain boundaries, thus improving crack resistance and compressive strength without significantly altering the intrinsic caloric performance of the alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure but suffers from poor structural integrity (cracking).
generation.intervention: Introduce 1–2 at.% of Cu as a microalloying element into the base alloy.
generation.conditions: Tests conducted under applied magnetic or pressure fields, temperature cycles and compressive loading that mirror previous studies on similar MM′X systems; the operational regimes should be comparable with those used for epoxy-containing and low-melting In composites.
generation.structural_mediator: Ductile nanoprecipitates that form at grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The Cu addition is expected to modify the microstructure by forming fine, ductile second phases which localize at grain boundaries. These nanoprecipitates can impede crack initiation and propagation by relieving localized stress concentrations. At the same time, because the primary caloric phase transformation remains unchanged in the alloy matrix, the caloric response should be largely preserved.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in compressive strength (targeting values above 200 MPa) and a reduction in crack propagation while maintaining the caloric effect within ±5% of that observed in the unalloyed sample.
generation.baseline: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits excellent caloric properties but fails under mechanical load due to cracking.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is valid under conditions similar to previous studies on MM′X materials (i.e., under comparable magnetic, pressure, temperature cycling, and mechanical load conditions) and assumes that the added Cu does not form undesired magnetic or brittle phases.
generation.uncertainty: The precise optimal Cu concentration, its distribution within the microstructure, and long-term stability under cyclic operation require further investigation. There is also some uncertainty about minor interactions that might subtly affect the caloric properties.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the baseline (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy and a second set with 1–2 at.% Cu added. Subject both sets to identical applied magnetic/pressure fields, thermal cycles, and compressive loading tests. Perform detailed microstructural analyses (using TEM or similar techniques) to identify the formation and distribution of nanoprecipitates at grain boundaries.
measurements: Compressive strength under standardized loading conditions
Caloric response (measured via entropy change ΔS or temperature change under applied-field conditions)
Microstructural characterization (grain boundary imaging and phase analysis)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Cu-doped samples show less than a ~15% improvement in compressive strength (relative to the baseline) or exhibit a caloric response that deviates by more than ±5% from that of the unalloyed material, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
